target.title: fix(firecrawl): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Firecrawl config field lookups use `"firecrawl" in <configObj>` to check whether a Firecrawl provider config block is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so a prototype-polluted property (e.g. via crafted `__proto__` in JSON reaching an `Object.assign` merge step in the config pipeline) is detected as a legitimate config entry.

This is the **pre-Zod validation boundary** — the raw POJO config object from `JSON5.parse()` before schema validation. The `in` checks operate on the raw object where prototype-chain properties survive until the `Object.hasOwn()` gate.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as explicit Firecrawl config entries.

### Evidence

**Config-loader path proof** — demonstrates that a crafted `__proto__` in JSON config reaches the firecrawl resolver through the pipeline's `Object.assign` merge step, and that `Object.hasOwn()` rejects the polluted property:

```
-- STEP 1 — Object.assign with __proto__ pollutes [[Prototype]] --

  JSON.parse result own keys:    [__proto__]
  parsedSource.__proto__:        {"firecrawl":{"apiKey":"POLLUTED_BY_ATTACKER"}}
  'firecrawl' in target:                true
  Object.hasOwn(target, "firecrawl"):     false

-- STEP 2 — in operator FOLLOWS prototype chain --

  Object.create({firecrawl:{apiKey:"ATTACKER_KEY"}})
  'firecrawl' in polluted obj:           true
  Object.hasOwn(polluted, "firecrawl"):    false
  => in operator returns true for proto-inherited properties

-- STEP 3 — Object.hasOwn checks ONLY own properties --

  Object.create (proto): 'firecrawl' in:  true
  Object.create (proto): hasOwn:            false
  Plain object (own):   'firecrawl' in:  true
  Plain object (own):   hasOwn:            true
  => Object.hasOwn rejects proto, accepts own

-- STEP 4 — Attack scenario summary --

  JSON config file:
    {"__proto__":{"firecrawl":{"apiKey":"MALICIOUS"}}}
          ↓
  JSON5.parse → Object.assign merge in pipeline
          ↓
  tools.web.search [[Prototype]] chain has firecrawl
          ↓
  BEFORE: "firecrawl" in searchRecord → true  → MALICIOUS KEY USED
  AFTER:  Object.hasOwn(searchRecord) → false → env KEY USED
          ↓
  fix: Object.hasOwn() blocks the entire chain

-- STEP 5 — Unit test verification --

  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/firecrawl/src/config-path-proof.test.ts
  6 tests passed:
    ✓ [STEP 1] Object.assign propagates __proto__
    ✓ [STEP 2] Proto-inherited firecrawl REACHES resolveFirecrawlSearchConfig
    ✓ [STEP 3] Own firecrawl config still works (backward compat)
    ✓ [STEP 4] Empty tools.web.search — no false positive
    ✓ [STEP 5] No tools.web.search — undefined input handled
    ✓ [STEP 6] Object.assign({}, raw) with __proto__ on tool config model

  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts
  11 tests passed (basic own-property safety)

CONTRACT VERIFICATION:
  Object.assign + JSON __proto__ key → pollutes [[Prototype]]:
    'firecrawl' in target   → true  (would accept attacker data)
    Object.hasOwn(target)     → false (rejects proto data)

  Config pipeline result:
    Proto-inherited firecrawl:  REJECTED by Object.hasOwn
    Own firecrawl config:       ACCEPTED (backward compat)
```

### Files changed
- `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts` — 2 replacements (search + fetch `Object.hasOwn`)
- `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts` — new test file (240 lines)
- `extensions/firecrawl/src/config-path-proof.test.ts` — new config-loader path proof (91 lines)
- `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` — updated test counts

target.title: Fix/OpenAI device code request timeout
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow only enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting. The three `fetch` calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request `AbortSignal` timeout, so a stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response could bypass that deadline and leave the CLI spinner stuck. A server that returned headers and then stalled the body could also escape an incomplete timeout catch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under the same `AbortSignal.timeout` (30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry on per-operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — one operation deadline for fetch + body read on user-code, poll, and token-exchange; poll retries on timeout within the 15-minute deadline
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code aborts with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - hung token exchange aborts with timeout error
  - success path asserts all three fetches carry an `AbortSignal`
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall: user-code / token-exchange abort with formatted timeout; poll retries and succeeds

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI Codex device-code login no longer leaves individual HTTP operations unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return, or returns headers and then stalls the body.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs device-code auth → `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `requestOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `exchangeOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `runOpenAICodexDeviceCodeRequest` (`fetch` + `readOpenAICodexDeviceBody` under `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production device-code helpers exercised via colocated Vitest against a real hanging `node:http` loopback that sends headers then a partial JSON prefix and never finishes the body. Only `AbortSignal.timeout` duration is shortened for deterministic proof; the production fetch+body composition and error/retry mapping stay unmocked.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Matches the existing 30s OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth token request timeout; uses `AbortSignal.timeout` like GitHub Copilot device-flow request timeouts. Does not migrate this path onto `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in this change.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, product checkout on branch `fix/openai-device-code-request-timeout`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
 ✓ aborts hung user-code requests instead of waiting forever 1ms
 ✓ retries device authorization polls after a per-request timeout 0ms
 ✓ aborts hung token exchange requests instead of waiting forever 0ms
 ✓ aborts when user-code headers arrive but the body never completes 31ms
 ✓ retries authorization polls after a post-header body stall 43ms
 ✓ aborts when token-exchange headers arrive but the body never completes 43ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
 Duration  1.37s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.53s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Hung user-code and token-exchange fetches abort with `OpenAI device code ... timed out after 30000ms`; a poll `TimeoutError` (including post-header body stall) is retried and the login can still succeed within the overall deadline. Real loopback partial-body stalls exercise production body consumption under the same operation signal.
- **What was not tested:** Live `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code` against a real stalled `auth.openai.com` endpoint.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`
